overview.intro:
Chapter 57 covers every textile floor covering: **hand-knotted rugs** (5701), **woven rugs** — kilims, dhurries, flatweaves, Wilton and machine-woven area rugs (5702), **tufted carpet and rugs**, carpet tiles and artificial turf (5703), **felt** floor coverings (5704) and other rugs and mats (5705). Its **74 tariff lines** run from Free to 8%: 33 are Free, hand-knotted wool rugs pay 4.5%, tufted wool and synthetic carpet 5.8%–6.7%, Wilton and velvet roll carpet 8%.

The U.S. imported **$3.40B** of these goods in 2025. **India** ($1.29B, 38%) and **Turkey** ($773M, 23%) supplied 61% of it, ahead of China, Vietnam, Egypt and Mexico. On top of the base rate comes the **extra duty by country**: since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff on 60 economies — **+10% for India and Pakistan, +12.5% for Turkey, Egypt, Vietnam and Thailand, 10% in total for the EU and 12.5% for Korea**. **China pays +37.5%** (List 3 plus the 2026 action), so Chinese tufted nylon carpet pays 44.2%. Nepal and Afghanistan are not among the 60 and pay only the base rate. USMCA goods from Mexico pay nothing; Canadian tufted carpet of 5703.39.20 owes a **50% Section 338 duty** even under USMCA. **Carpets of Iranian origin cannot be imported at all** (31 CFR 560.201), and every rug sold in the U.S. must meet the CPSC flammability standards.

productGroups.label: Hand-knotted carpets and rugs (Persian-style, oriental)
productGroups.blurb: Hand-knotted (and other knotted) carpets and rugs — Persian-style, oriental and tribal rugs. Wool rugs are 5701.10.90 at 4.5%, hand-hooked knotted wool rugs and alpaca- or llama-hair rugs Free; silk, cotton and man-made-fiber knotted rugs (5701.90) are Free.

productGroups.label: Woven rugs and carpets: kilims, dhurries, flatweaves, Wilton and machine-woven
productGroups.blurb: Woven floor coverings: kilims, soumaks and dhurries (5702.10, Free), coir mats, Wilton, Axminster-type and velvet carpet, and machine-woven area rugs. Made-up woven pile rugs of wool or man-made fibers are Free; roll goods pay 4%–8%; flat-woven cotton rugs 6.8%, wool 3.6%–6.3%, man-made 2.7%–4.7%.

productGroups.label: Tufted carpets and rugs, carpet tiles and artificial turf
productGroups.blurb: Tufted carpets and rugs — hand-tufted and machine-tufted area rugs, broadloom, carpet tiles and artificial turf. The most-rated group: wool 6%, nylon 6.7% (hand-hooked 5.8%), polypropylene and polyester 6%, other fibers 3.8%.

productGroups.label: Felt carpets and carpet tiles (not tufted or flocked)
productGroups.blurb: Felt carpets and tiles, not tufted or flocked: tiles of 0.3 m² or less pay 4.7%; larger tiles and other felt floor coverings are Free.

productGroups.label: Other floor coverings: braided, needlepoint, coir and other mats
productGroups.blurb: Other floor coverings, whether or not made up: coir mats Free; braided, needlepoint and other rugs and mats 3.3%.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** For the purposes of this chapter, the term "carpets and other textile floor coverings" means floor coverings in which textile materials serve as the exposed surface of the article when in use and includes articles having the characteristics of textile floor coverings but intended for use for other purposes.

**Note 2.** This chapter does not cover floor covering underlays.

The Section XI (textiles) notes also apply. Note 7 decides when a rug is "made up" (cut to shape, hemmed or with a knotted fringe, assembled), which splits several 5702 lines. Subheading note 2(B)(b): for textile products with a ground fabric and a pile or looped surface, no account is taken of the ground fabric — so a carpet's fiber is that of its pile.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
Chapter 57 has no additional U.S. notes of its own. **Section XI additional U.S. note 2**: "certified hand-loomed and folklore" products (5701.10.13, 5702.10.10, 5702.91.20) are those certified by an official of a government agency of the producing country under procedures established by USTR.

**Footnote to 5701.10.40, 5701.10.90 and 5701.90.20**: see 9817.57.01 — needle-craft display models of completed mass-produced kits, primarily hand stitched, enter Free.

The three-digit numbers in brackets — (369) cotton, (465) wool, (665) man-made fibers — are textile category numbers used to monitor shipments.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 57: Carpets & Rugs — Tariff Updates

seo.title: Rug & Carpet Tariff Updates 2026: HTS Chapter 57 — Section 301, China, India, Turkey, Iran Ban | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 57 rugs and carpets since January 2025: base rates unchanged, IEEPA and Section 122 duties ended, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (India +10%, Turkey +12.5%, EU 10%), China +37.5%, Canada Section 338 on tufted carpet, the Nepal program lapse and the Iranian carpet ban — with Federal Register citations.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 57 base rate changed**: all 74 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates, from Free to 8%.

Everything that changed sits on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA duties reached rugs from almost every country — 15% for Turkey, 19% for Pakistan, 20% for Vietnam, 15% in total for the EU from August 7, 2025, 50% for India from August 27, and up to 125% plus 20% for China in April–May 2025, on top of the 25% List 3 duty. The IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff**: +10% for India, Pakistan and the UK, +12.5% for Turkey, Egypt and Vietnam, 10% in total for the EU. China still pays the **25% List 3 duty** on every line, 37.5% in all. Since **August 22, 2026** Canadian tufted carpet of 5703.39.20 pays a **50% Section 338 duty**, even under USMCA. The Nepal duty-free program expired December 31, 2025, and Iranian carpets remain banned.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 57 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 List 3, the Canada Section 338 duty on 5703.39.20, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. The Nepal program and the OFAC ban on Iranian carpets are listed for reference. No Section 232 action and no antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 57 product. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.44). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). India has no exception list. The IEEPA duties on India — 25% reciprocal from August 7, 2025 plus 25% from August 27, 2025 — ended in February 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A hand-knotted wool rug from India (5701.10.90, 4.5%) pays 14.5%; a hand-tufted wool rug (5703.10.80, 6%) 16%; a hand-woven cotton dhurrie (5702.99.05, 6.8%) 16.8%; kilims and made-up woven wool rugs (Free) 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 12.5% (9903.05.79). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Turkey has no exception list. The 15% IEEPA reciprocal duty (9903.02.64, from August 7, 2025) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Machine-woven polypropylene area rugs, made up (5702.42.20, Free), pay 12.5%; tufted polypropylene or polyester carpet (5703.39.20, 6%) 18.5%; hand-knotted wool rugs 17%.

inEffect.exemption: Two Section 301 duties stack: +12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31) and +25% under List 3 (9903.88.03), which covers every Chapter 57 subheading. None of the China exclusions in force (U.S. note 20(vvv) and (www), through November 9, 2026) covers a Chapter 57 product; the older rug exclusions printed in note 20 have expired. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026, and USTR's four-year review kept List 3 in place.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese tufted nylon carpet and carpet tiles (6.7%) pay 44.2%, artificial turf 43.5%–44.2%, hand-knotted wool rugs 42%, Free lines 37.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 12.5% (9903.05.84). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The 20% IEEPA reciprocal duty (9903.02.69) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese tufted rugs pay 18.5%–19.2%, woven made-up rugs 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 12.5% (9903.05.36). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Egypt has no exception list. The 10% IEEPA baseline duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Egyptian machine-woven polypropylene rugs (Free) pay 12.5%; tufted rugs 18.5%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94); others pay +10% (9903.05.55). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Mexico is not subject to the Canada Section 338 duties. The 25% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA-qualifying rugs and carpet from Mexico pay nothing; non-qualifying goods pay the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: For EU goods whose base rate is under 10% — every Chapter 57 line — the total is 10% (9903.05.39, U.S. note 52(k)). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The EU exception list (note 52(j)(2)) names no Chapter 57 line. This replaced the 15%-in-total IEEPA rate (9903.02.20), which ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Belgian machine-woven rugs and Dutch or German carpet tiles pay 10% of value — $1,000 on $10,000 — whatever their base rate.

inEffect.exemption: Korean goods pay 12.5% in total in place of the base rate when the base rate is lower (9903.05.71). Every Chapter 57 line is below 12.5%, so Korean rugs and carpet pay 12.5%, with or without a KORUS claim (U.S. note 52(a)). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Korea has no exception list. The 15% IEEPA reciprocal duty (9903.02.56) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Korean tufted carpet and carpet tiles pay 12.5% of value — $1,250 on $10,000.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 12.5% (9903.05.77). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The 19% IEEPA reciprocal duty (9903.02.61) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Thai machine-woven rugs (Free) pay 12.5%; tufted rugs 18.5%–19.2%.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.81). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The UK exception list (note 52(j)(1)) has no Chapter 57 line. The 10% IEEPA reciprocal duty ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: British Wilton or Axminster-type woven wool carpet (5702.31.10, 8%) pays 18%; tufted wool carpet 16%.

inEffect.exemption: Base rate + 10% (9903.05.62). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The 19% IEEPA reciprocal duty (9903.02.51) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: A hand-knotted wool rug from Pakistan pays 14.5%; hand-knotted rugs of silk or cotton (5701.90, Free) 10%.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariff (non-USMCA goods) + Section 338 duty (5703.39.20, USMCA or not)
inEffect.exemption: Two measures. The 2026 Section 301 duty (+10%, 9903.05.29) does not apply to USMCA-qualifying goods (9903.05.93). The Section 338 duty (+50%, from August 22, 2026, 9903.03.14) applies to tufted carpet of 5703.39.20 — tufted floor coverings of man-made fibers other than nylon (polypropylene, polyester), other than turf and hand-hooked goods — and U.S. note 51(a) says it applies even when USMCA is claimed. The September 15, 2026 list revisions and the September 29, 2026 import bans changed no Chapter 57 entry. The 35% IEEPA duty on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: USMCA-qualifying Canadian polyester or polypropylene tufted carpet pays 50%; non-qualifying, 66% (6% + 10% + 50%). Other Canadian rugs pay nothing under USMCA.

inEffect.measure: Section 301 tariffs: Brazil action plus 2026 forced-labor action
inEffect.exemption: +25% under the Brazil action from July 22, 2026 (9903.05.01) and +12.5% under the 2026 action from July 24, 2026 (9903.05.27). The Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)) names no Chapter 57 line. The 40% IEEPA duty on Brazil (Executive Order 14323) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian rugs and carpet pay 37.5% on top of the base rate.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (incl. Bangladesh, Morocco, Taiwan, Jordan, Guatemala, El Salvador)
inEffect.now: +10% or 10% (in place of base) or +12.5% or 12.5% (in place of base)
inEffect.exemption: Rates by country: Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Indonesia +10%, Morocco +12.5%, Taiwan 10% in total (9903.05.76). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). Three country exception lists in U.S. note 52(j) cover **every Chapter 57 subheading**: Jordan (9903.06.20), and Guatemala (9903.06.06) and El Salvador (9903.06.09) when CAFTA-DR is claimed — so their rugs pay no Section 301 duty. CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR are also exempt (note 52(i), 9903.05.95). Countries outside the 60 economies — Nepal and Afghanistan among them — pay only the base rate. Iranian-origin carpets cannot be imported at all: the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR 560.201) bar goods of Iranian origin, and the general license that allowed Persian carpets from 2016 ended with a wind-down on August 6, 2018. The ban is an OFAC rule, not a tariff, so the duty calculator does not model it.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Bangladeshi jute or cotton rugs pay the base rate plus 10%; Jordanian rugs and CAFTA-DR rugs from Guatemala or El Salvador pay nothing extra; Nepalese and Afghan hand-knotted wool rugs pay only 4.5%.

changes.title: No Chapter 57 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 74 Chapter 57 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition, and no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 continues after the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their 2026 anniversaries because domestic industries asked for them to continue. For Chapter 57 this keeps +25% (List 3) on every carpet, rug, mat and artificial-turf line.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 lists revised; Chapter 57 entry unchanged
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 added and removed provisions on the 9903.03.12 and 9903.03.14 lists. 5703.39.20 stays on the list, no other Chapter 57 provision was added, and the September 29, 2026 Canadian import bans name no Chapter 57 product.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty takes effect on tufted carpet (5703.39.20)
changes.detail: 50% on listed products of Canada after a 3-day suspension lapsed. One Chapter 57 subheading is on the motor-vehicle list (9903.03.14): 5703.39.20, tufted carpets and rugs of man-made fibers other than nylon (polypropylene, polyester), other than turf and hand-hooked goods. Unlike the Section 301 duty, it applies to USMCA-qualifying goods too (U.S. note 51(a)).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover all of Chapter 57
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84). No Chapter 57 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). EU goods pay 10% in total. India, Pakistan and the UK +10%; Turkey, Egypt and Vietnam +12.5%. Jordanian rugs, and CAFTA-DR rugs from Guatemala and El Salvador, are exempt on every Chapter 57 line (note 52(j)). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Nepal, Afghanistan and Iran are not among the 60.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 57 line is on the Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% forced-labor tariff (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: CPSC certificate data now filed electronically at entry
changes.detail: Carpets and rugs must meet the CPSC flammability standards (16 CFR 1630 and 1631), so importers issue a General Certificate of Conformity. From July 8, 2026 the certificate data must be filed electronically with CBP at entry (January 8, 2027 for goods entered from a foreign-trade zone). No duty changes.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still remove the base rate and the Section 301 duty on Mexican and Canadian rugs — but not the Section 338 duty on 5703.39.20.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 57 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. The 25% reciprocal rate on India ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. In Chapter 57, AGOA (SPI D) covers nine lines — hand-woven and flat-woven rugs (5702.50.20, 5702.91.30, 5702.92.10, 5702.99.05, 5702.99.20), hand-hooked tufted rugs (5703.10.20, 5703.29.10, 5703.39.10) and tufted rugs of other textile materials (5703.90.00). GSP (SPI A, A*) remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Nepal Preference Program (NP) expired
changes.detail: The program that let Nepal ship hand-knotted wool rugs (5701.10.90) and 12 other Chapter 57 lines duty-free (SPI NP) ended after December 31, 2025, as the statute required. The NP code is still printed in the Special column but no longer applies: a Nepalese hand-knotted wool rug now pays the 4.5% General rate. Nepal is not one of the 60 Section 301 economies, so nothing is added.
changes.now: General rate (4.5% on hand-knotted wool rugs)

changes.title: Scheduled: Section 301 tariff on products of Nicaragua
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that pay the column 1-general rate (that is, not entered under CAFTA-DR) will pay +10% (9903.89.01) from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. Today Nicaragua pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.58).

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian rugs, on top of the base rate — 54.5% on a hand-knotted wool rug. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates for goods entered from August 7, 2025: Turkey and Afghanistan +15%, Pakistan +19%, Vietnam and Bangladesh +20%, India +25%, the UK +10%; countries not listed, such as Egypt and Nepal, kept +10%. EU goods with a column 1 rate under 15% paid 15% in total (9903.02.20) — every Chapter 57 line. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. Chinese tufted nylon carpet then paid 6.7% + 25% (List 3) + 20% + 10% = 61.7% until November 9, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025. With the 20% fentanyl duty and the 25% List 3 duty, Chinese tufted nylon carpet paid 176.7% until May 13, 2025.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 57 product was exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the List 3 duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China List 3 duty raised to 25%
changes.detail: USTR raised the List 3 duty (9903.88.03) from 10% to 25%. List 3 covers every Chapter 57 subheading, and the rate has applied ever since.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 reaches all carpets and rugs
changes.detail: The third China Section 301 list put +10% on every Chapter 57 subheading — knotted, woven, tufted and felt carpets, artificial turf and other floor coverings.

changes.title: Iranian carpet imports banned again
changes.detail: After the United States left the Iran nuclear agreement, OFAC narrowed the carpet and foodstuff general license (31 CFR 560.534) to a wind-down that ended at 11:59 p.m. EDT on August 6, 2018. Since then the 31 CFR 560.201 import ban applies to Iranian-origin carpets of Chapter 57 (and antique carpets of 9706), whether shipped from Iran or a third country. Used carpets that are part of an arriving traveler's household effects are still allowed (31 CFR 560.524).

changes.title: Iranian carpet license revoked (2010–2016)
changes.detail: OFAC revoked the 2000 general license for Iranian carpets and foodstuffs; it was restored on January 21, 2016 (81 FR 3330). The license had allowed Persian carpets since April 28, 2000 (65 FR 25642).

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 57 goods were **$3.40B in 2025**, 6.4% less than the $3.63B of 2024 and below the $4.22B peak of 2021. Woven rugs (5702) made up 45% ($1.55B) — most of it **machine-woven pile area rugs of man-made fibers (5702.42)**, $892M, the largest single product. Tufted carpet, rugs, tiles and turf (5703) were $1.13B and hand-knotted rugs (5701) $357M.

**India** ($1.29B, 38%) is the largest supplier, with hand-knotted, hand-tufted and woven rugs across every heading. **Turkey** ($773M, -12.1%) ships mainly machine-woven polypropylene and polyester area rugs. **China** fell 37.0% to $295M, while **Vietnam** grew 41.8% to $244M and **Thailand** doubled to $54.2M. **Egypt** ($127M) and **Mexico** ($111M) follow; hand-knotted rugs also come from **Nepal** ($50.5M), **Pakistan** ($41.9M) and **Afghanistan** ($6.8M). UN Comtrade shows just $10K from Iran, whose carpets are banned.

The figures are annual and stop at 2025, before the 2026 tariff changes (the end of the IEEPA duties in February, the Section 301 tariffs from July 24, 2026, the lapse of Nepal's duty-free program on January 1, 2026 and the Canada Section 338 duty from August 22); they do not show what those changes did. Duty-collected figures are not available from an official source yet.

Chapter 57 base rates are modest — Free to 8% — so the **country of origin** decides most of the cost. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — taken from the current tariff schedule.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** that started July 24, 2026: **+10% for India, Pakistan and the UK**, **+12.5% for Turkey, Egypt, Vietnam and Thailand**, **10% in total for the Netherlands, Belgium and the rest of the EU**, 12.5% in total for South Korea. **China adds 37.5%**. **Nepal and Afghanistan pay only the base rate** — 4.5% on a hand-knotted wool rug. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico pay nothing; from Canada nothing except the **50% Section 338 duty on tufted carpet of 5703.39.20**, which no USMCA claim removes. Iranian carpets cannot be imported.

Rugs need no import license, but four sets of rules apply at or after entry. **Flammability**: every carpet or rug sold for use as a floor covering must pass the CPSC pill test — 16 CFR 1630 for large carpets, 1631 for small rugs (no side over 6 ft, 24 sq ft or less), and small rugs that fail must carry a permanent "FLAMMABLE" label. The importer certifies compliance in a General Certificate of Conformity, filed electronically with the entry since July 8, 2026. **Labeling**: fiber content of the face or pile and the country of origin under the FTC Textile Rules, plus CBP origin marking. **Origin**: a carpet's origin is where it was knotted, woven or tufted (19 CFR 102.21). **Sanctions**: carpets of Iranian origin are banned, wherever they ship from.

On cost, the construction and fiber decide the base rate (Free to 8%), and the country of origin decides the extra duty (+0% for Nepal, +10% for India, +37.5% for China). Each lever below depends on a document, listed with its regulation.

levers.title: Classify by construction, make-up and pile fiber
levers.saves: Up to 8 points of base rate: woven pile rugs of man-made fibers are Free when made up (5702.42) but 7%–8% as unfinished roll goods (5702.32); hand-knotted rugs are Free in silk or cotton (5701.90) and 4.5% in wool (5701.10.90); tufted rugs pay 3.8%–6.7%
levers.appliesTo: All lines — the heading follows the construction (knotted 5701, woven 5702, tufted 5703, felt 5704, other 5705), and the subheading the fiber of the pile or face and whether the rug is made up
levers.document: Construction and fiber details on the invoice: knotted, woven or tufted, hand or machine made, pile and backing fibers by weight, size and finishing (bound or fringed edges make a rug "made up", Section XI note 7).
levers.caveat: The pile decides the fiber: for carpets with a pile, the ground fabric or backing is ignored (Section XI subheading note 2(B)(b)). Tufting with a power-driven gun is not "hand-hooked". Floor-covering underlays are not Chapter 57 (chapter note 2).

citations.label: HTSUS Section XI notes 7 and subheading note 2

levers.title: Know the country of origin — it sets the extra duty
levers.saves: The gap between country rates: nothing extra for Nepal or Afghanistan, +10% for India and Pakistan, +12.5% for Turkey and Egypt, 10% in total for the EU, +37.5% for China
levers.document: Origin follows 19 CFR 102.21(e): a carpet originates where it was knotted, woven or tufted from yarn. Washing, clipping, binding, latex backing or repairing in another country does not change it. The manufacturer ID (MID) on the entry must name the company that made the rug.
levers.caveat: Shipping through a lower-rate country does not change origin, and false origin claims are a customs violation. Iranian-origin carpets are banned even if finished or shipped elsewhere (31 CFR 560.306).

levers.title: Use the note 52(j) exception lists and the CAFTA-DR textile exemption
levers.saves: The 10% Section 301 duty on every Chapter 57 line
levers.appliesTo: All 74 lines for products of Jordan (9903.06.20), and of Guatemala (9903.06.06) and El Salvador (9903.06.09) entered under CAFTA-DR; CAFTA-DR textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (9903.05.95)
levers.document: The exemption heading reported with the entry line, and for CAFTA-DR goods a valid origin claim with the SPI "P".
levers.caveat: The EU, UK, Swiss and other exception lists name no Chapter 57 line. The calculator models the Jordan, Guatemala and El Salvador lists but not note 52(i), which defines its goods by a WTO textile annex.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)(6)–(7), (j)(13)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on rugs made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 8%) and the 10% Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: All lines, for goods that qualify as originating — generally carpets made in North America from North American yarn (General Note 11, Chapter 57 rules)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the SPI "S" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on tufted carpet of 5703.39.20 (U.S. note 51(a)). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Claim an FTA or AGOA rate where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate: up to 8% (Wilton and velvet carpet), 6.8% (cotton flatweaves), 6%–6.7% (tufted carpet), 4.5% (hand-knotted wool)
levers.appliesTo: The 41 dutiable lines, for goods of Korea, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Israel, Jordan, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman, Singapore and CAFTA-DR countries; AGOA countries (through December 31, 2026) on nine woven and tufted lines
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement and the SPI on the entry line (KR, AU, CL, CO, PE, PA, IL, JO, MA, BH, OM, SG, P, D).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)) unless a note 52(j) list or note 52(i) covers the goods. GSP (A, A*) has been expired since December 31, 2020 and the Nepal program (NP) since December 31, 2025, although both codes are still printed.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Certify hand-loomed and folklore rugs
levers.saves: 4.3 points of base rate on hand-woven flat wool rugs (5702.91.20 Free instead of 5702.91.30 at 4.3%)
levers.appliesTo: Hand-woven wool rugs, made up, not of pile construction; the other "certified hand-loomed and folklore" lines (5701.10.13 alpaca-hair rugs, 5702.10.10 kilims) are Free either way
levers.document: A certificate from an official of a government agency of the producing country, issued under procedures set up by USTR (Section XI additional U.S. note 2).
levers.caveat: Only countries with a certification arrangement can issue the certificate. The extra duty by country still applies.

citations.label: HTSUS Section XI additional U.S. note 2

levers.title: Enter carpet samples as samples
levers.saves: All duty — the base rate and the Section 301, China and Canada duties
levers.appliesTo: Carpet swatches and sample tiles valued at $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, used only to solicit orders
levers.document: Entry under 9811.00.60 with the samples marked or mutilated as the heading requires.
levers.caveat: Usable rugs and full-size tiles sent as samples are classified in Chapter 57 like any other rug. U.S. notes 20, 51 and 52 exempt goods properly entered under Chapter 98 from those extra duties.

provisions.text: Samples valued not over $1 each, or marked, torn, perforated or otherwise treated so they are unsuitable for sale, used only for soliciting orders for products of foreign countries

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20(a), 51, 52(a)

levers.title: Get a binding classification ruling where the line decides the rate
levers.saves: Certainty on the splits that move the rate: knotted vs. tufted, hand-hooked vs. gun-tufted, made up vs. roll goods, wool vs. man-made pile, Wilton/velvet vs. other woven carpet
levers.appliesTo: Any line where construction or fiber is in doubt — especially blended piles and hand-tufted goods
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing construction, fiber content by weight, size and finishing (19 CFR part 177).
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a different construction may need its own.

levers.title: Claim drawback when rugs are exported
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties, on imported rugs or carpet re-exported
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or destroyed under CBP supervision
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded.

rules.title: Large carpets and rugs (one side over 6 ft and over 24 sq ft, and carpet tiles meant to be installed as larger areas) must pass the FF 1-70 pill test: at least 7 of 8 specimens. One-of-a-kind antique, oriental or hide rugs may be excluded under CPSC conditions

Small carpets and rugs (no side over 6 ft, 24 sq ft or less) are tested under FF 2-70; a rug that fails may be sold only with a permanent label: "FLAMMABLE (FAILS U.S. DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE STANDARD FF 2-70): SHOULD NOT BE USED NEAR SOURCES OF IGNITION"

General Certificate of Conformity for the flammability standard, issued by the importer; its data filed electronically with CBP at entry from July 8, 2026 (January 8, 2027 for goods from a foreign-trade zone)

Textile Fiber Products Identification Act: floor coverings sold onward must show fiber content and country of origin; on rugs with a backing the content refers to the face or pile only ("100% Wool Pile")
Textile country of origin: a carpet or rug (5701–5705) originates where it was made from yarn of another chapter — knotted, woven or tufted; finishing elsewhere does not change it
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the company that made the rug on every commercial entry; entry is denied for textiles from companies named by CITA for illegal transshipment
Country-of-origin marking on each rug; Native American-style rugs must be marked indelibly — a sewn-in label counts
Carpets of Iranian origin may not be imported, from Iran or a third country, without an OFAC license; arriving travelers' used household rugs are exempt

Goods made by forced or indentured child labor may not be imported; we found no CBP withhold release order or finding naming carpets, and in 2016 Labor, State and DHS declined to add Indian carpets to the Executive Order 13126 list

groups.label: Hand-knotted carpets and rugs (Persian-style, oriental)
groups.note: Hand-knotted wool rugs are 5701.10.90 (4.5%); silk, cotton and man-made-fiber knotted rugs are Free. Origin is where the rug was knotted. Iranian-origin Persian rugs are banned; Persian-design rugs knotted in India, Pakistan, Nepal or Turkey are not Iranian.

groups.label: Woven rugs and carpets: kilims, dhurries, flatweaves, Wilton and machine-woven
groups.note: Kilims, dhurries, coir and jute rugs are Free; made-up woven pile rugs of wool or man-made fibers are Free, unfinished roll goods 4%–8%. Certified folklore hand-woven wool rugs (5702.91.20) are Free instead of 4.3%.

groups.label: Tufted carpets and rugs, carpet tiles and artificial turf
groups.note: The highest-rated group: 5.8%–6.7% on tufted wool, nylon and polypropylene rugs, carpet tiles and turf (3.8% for other fibers). Canadian 5703.39.20 pays the 50% Section 338 duty even under USMCA. Gun-tufted rugs are not "hand-hooked".

groups.label: Felt carpets and carpet tiles (not tufted or flocked)
groups.note: Felt tiles of 0.3 m² or less pay 4.7%; larger felt tiles and other felt floor coverings are Free.

groups.label: Other floor coverings: braided, needlepoint, coir and other mats
groups.note: Coir mats are Free; other floor coverings (braided, needlepoint and other) 3.3%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code (tariff code) for rugs and carpets?
faqs.answer: Rugs and carpets are HTS Chapter 57, by construction: 5701 knotted (hand-knotted) rugs, 5702 woven rugs (kilims, dhurries, flatweaves, machine-woven area rugs, Wilton), 5703 tufted carpet, rugs, tiles and turf, 5704 felt, 5705 other floor coverings. The fiber of the pile then picks the 8- and 10-digit line. Base rates run from Free to 8%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for hand-knotted and hand-tufted rugs?
searchedAs: hand knotted wool rug hs code
indian hand knotted carpets hs code
hand tufted carpet us hts code
faqs.answer: Hand-knotted wool rugs are 5701.10.90.00 (4.5%); hand-knotted rugs of silk, cotton or man-made fibers are 5701.90.10 (Free). Hand-tufted rugs made with a tufting gun are tufted carpet of 5703: wool 5703.10.80 (6%), nylon 5703.29.20 (6.7%), polyester or polypropylene 5703.39.20 (6%). Only tufts inserted by hand or a non-powered tool count as "hand-hooked" (5703.10.20, 6%).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for wool, jute and cotton rugs?
faqs.answer: It depends on construction. Kilims, soumaks and similar hand-woven rugs are 5702.10 (Free). Woven jute rugs are 5702.39.10 or 5702.49.15 (Free). Flat-woven cotton rugs and dhurries are 5702.99.05 (hand-woven) or 5702.99.15 (6.8%). Woven wool rugs are 5702.31, 5702.41 or 5702.91 (Free to 8%); tufted wool rugs 5703.10 (6%). A tufted cotton bath rug is 5703.90.00 (3.8%).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for carpet tiles and artificial turf?
faqs.answer: Tufted carpet tiles are 5703.29.20.10 (nylon, 6.7%) or 5703.39.20.30 (other man-made fibers, 6%), for pieces of 5.25 m² or less. Artificial turf is 5703.21.00 (nylon, 6.7%) or 5703.31.00 (other man-made fibers, 6%). Felt tiles are 5704 (4.7% up to 0.3 m², otherwise Free). From China add 37.5%.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on rugs from India?
searchedAs: tariff on rug from india to usa
are there tariffs on rugs from india
faqs.answer: Indian rugs pay the base rate plus 10% Section 301 (9903.05.44) since July 24, 2026: 14.5% on a hand-knotted wool rug, 16% on a hand-tufted wool rug, 16.8% on a cotton dhurrie, 10% on Free lines such as kilims and made-up woven rugs. The IEEPA duties — 50% from August 27, 2025 — ended in February 2026.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on rugs from Turkey?
faqs.answer: Turkish goods pay the base rate plus 12.5% (9903.05.79): 12.5% on machine-woven polypropylene or polyester area rugs (5702.42, Free), 18.5% on tufted polypropylene carpet, 17% on hand-knotted wool rugs. Turkey has no Section 301 exception list. The 15% IEEPA duty ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on carpets and rugs from China?
faqs.answer: Every Chapter 57 line from China pays 25% under Section 301 List 3 (9903.88.03) plus 12.5% under the 2026 action (9903.05.31), on top of the base rate: 44.2% on tufted nylon carpet and tiles, 43.5% on polypropylene turf, 42% on hand-knotted wool rugs, 37.5% on Free lines. No product exclusion covers a rug. The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: Are Persian rugs illegal in the U.S.?
searchedAs: are persian rugs illegal in the us
why are persian rugs illegal in america
can you import rugs from iran
can you bring persian rug from iran to us
faqs.answer: Owning or reselling a Persian rug already in the U.S. is not illegal, but importing a carpet of Iranian origin is: the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR 560.201) bar Iranian-origin goods, from Iran or a third country. The general license that allowed Iranian carpets from January 2016 ended August 6, 2018. Used rugs in an arriving traveler's household effects are exempt (31 CFR 560.524). "Persian-style" rugs knotted in India, Pakistan, Nepal or Turkey are not Iranian.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on rugs in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. On top of base rates of Free to 8%, the 2026 Section 301 tariff adds 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies (10% in total for the EU, 12.5% for Korea), China pays 37.5% and Brazil 37.5%. Nepal and Afghanistan pay only the base rate. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.

faqs.question: What are the flammability requirements for carpets and rugs?
searchedAs: what are the flammability requirements for carpets
faqs.answer: Carpets and rugs must pass the CPSC methenamine pill test: 16 CFR 1630 (FF 1-70) for rugs with a side over 6 ft and more than 24 sq ft, 16 CFR 1631 (FF 2-70) for smaller ones — 7 of 8 specimens must pass. A small rug that fails must carry a permanent "FLAMMABLE" warning label. Importers certify in a General Certificate of Conformity, eFiled at entry since July 8, 2026.

faqs.question: How is the country of origin of a rug determined?
faqs.answer: Under 19 CFR 102.21(e), a carpet or rug of 5701–5705 originates where it was knotted, woven or tufted from yarn. Washing, clipping, binding or backing in another country does not change it. The origin sets the extra duty and must be on the CBP marking and the FTC label.

faqs.question: Do carpet samples pay duty?
faqs.answer: Samples worth $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, and used only to solicit orders, enter Free under 9811.00.60 — which also takes them outside the Section 301, China and Canada extra duties. Usable rugs and full tiles sent as samples are classified in Chapter 57.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import rugs from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $3.40B of Chapter 57 goods: India $1.29B (38%), Turkey $773M (23%), China $295M, Vietnam $244M, Egypt $127M and Mexico $111M. Machine-woven pile area rugs (5702.42) were the largest product at $892M.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on rugs from Nepal, Pakistan and Afghanistan?
faqs.answer: Nepal and Afghanistan are not among the 60 Section 301 economies, so a hand-knotted wool rug pays only the 4.5% base rate (Nepal's duty-free program expired December 31, 2025). Pakistan pays +10%: 14.5% on a hand-knotted wool rug, 10% on Free lines.
